More than 50 tractor-trailers took part in a truckers' protest in Nuevo Laredo on Monday, Oct. 26, parking on the Carretera Nacional at kilometer 17 while leaving one lane open in each direction, rather than blocking the World Trade Bridge, according to El Mañana de Nuevo Laredo.

The Nuevo Laredo action was part of a national freight stoppage organized by the National Chamber of Freight Transportation (CANACAR) and other transport groups that began Monday, Oct. 26. The groups cited highway robberies, extortion, violence against drivers, deteriorating roads and rising operating costs, along with proposed 2027 tax changes that could limit eligibility for a credit on highway toll costs, according to industry and government accounts of the dispute.

Nuevo Laredo matters to the dispute because it sits across the border from Laredo, the nation's leading inland port of entry, and freight movement through the corridor is central to cross-border trade. El Mañana described the Nuevo Laredo action as a peaceful stoppage organized by four cargo-transport associations, and said the World Trade Bridge was not blocked and remained busy, with freight crossings continuing. CANACAR delegate Ricardo Pillado Herrejón was cited in the report.

After meeting federal officials on Tuesday, CANACAR and other groups agreed to remove blockades and pause the demonstrations while talks continue, with working groups set to address highway security, infrastructure, tax matters, social security and working conditions, according to reports on the agreement. The pause does not settle the truckers' demands.

Sources:

  • El Mañana de Nuevo Laredo, "Así fue la protesta de 50 tráileres en Nuevo Laredo; paran en la carretera, no en el puente," Oct. 27, 2026
  • FreightWaves, "Mexican truckers launch national strike over highway security, rising costs," Oct. 26, 2026

title: Nuevo Laredo truckers protest: 50 trailers stop on highway, not bridge, as national strike pauses for talks
